name: Jean A. Saludadez
half:
Jean A. Saludadez has advised 37 theses in this repository between 2018 and 2026. Their research focus and supervision patterns show a strong emphasis on communication studies, which accounts for 21 items, followed by governance and public policy with 13 items, and culture and identity with 11 items. Other supervised topics include gender and inclusion, community development, arts and creative practice, journalism and news media, youth and family, social media, and online and distance learning. They have an advisee in the latest year, 2026.

Supervision topics range from investigating communicative practices of educators in integrating broadcasting experience to teaching documentary filmmaking to amplify marginalized voices, to examining the strategic relevance of amphibious warfare in ASEAN through discourse analysis. They have advised work on automating repository management and knowledge sharing in BPO support services, public-private partnerships in R&D, and integrating ASEAN perspectives in social studies education. Their supervision includes studies on laboratory resilience, online collaboration for telework, digital ageism on Facebook, and teacher authority in AI-infused classrooms. They have also overseen research on child marriage, student confession pages, diasporic communication, and the social construction of inclusivity on digital platforms. Evidence for some specific research summaries is thin, as several entries provided only title and acceptance pages.

Jean A. Saludadez has advised 37 theses in this repository between 2018 and 2026. Their research focus and supervision patterns show a heavy emphasis on communication studies, which accounts for 21 items. Other significant areas of supervision include governance and public policy (13), culture and identity (11), gender and inclusion (5), community development (4), arts and creative practice (4), journalism and news media (3), youth and family (3), social media (3), and online and distance learning (3). Their own articles in this repository focus on gender and inclusion, governance and public policy, culture and identity, and climate and disaster.

The adviser has supervised a wide range of topics. In the area of communication studies, they have overseen research on the communicative practices of an educator integrating broadcasting experience into documentary filmmaking pedagogy, the communicative construction of teacher identity for non-native English-speaking teachers in the United States, and the communicative constitution of hospitality organizations through guest service. They have also supervised studies on the communicative practices of women in information technology leadership, the communicative practices of Yakan weavers, and the communicative practices of rice farmers in Midsayap, Cotabato.

In governance and public policy, they have advised work on the strategic relevance of amphibious warfare in ASEAN, public-private partnerships in R&D, the integration of ASEAN perspectives in social studies education, and the authority of non-human agents in peace process documents. Their supervision also extends to gender and inclusion, including studies on digital ageism and the communicative marginalization of older persons, the social construction of inclusivity for people with dwarfism on digital platforms, and gender equality law and policies as perceived by Japanese women.

Other supervised research areas include community development, such as studies on how online collaboration makes telework possible and the branding of non-profit organizations on digital platforms. They have supervised work on arts and creative practice, including the agency of film in history education and the communicative practices of women IT leaders. In the realm of journalism and news media, they have overseen research on the framing of the proposed creation of the Autonomous Region of the Cordillera by community newspapers. Their supervision also covers youth and family, including studies on child marriage and cyberbullying.

Evidence for some research areas is thin due to limited available information in the repository. For several theses from 2018 to 2025, the full research content, including methodology and findings, was not provided in the repository, leaving the specific research details for those items unconfirmed. However, the breadth of topics supervised from 2018 to 2026 demonstrates a diverse range of communicative and social research interests.
two:
Jean A. Saludadez has advised 37 theses in this repository between 2018 and 2026. Their research focus and supervision patterns show a strong emphasis on communication studies, which accounts for 21 items. Other significant areas of interest include governance and public policy (13 items), culture and identity (11 items), and gender and inclusion (5 items). They have also supervised work related to community development (4 items), arts and creative practice (4 items), journalism and news media (3 items), youth and family (3 items), social media (3 items), and online and distance learning (3 items). Their own published articles in this repository focus on gender and inclusion within the context of governance and public policy, specifically examining gender voices in disaster risk reduction management discourse and gender representation within Indigenous Peoples Civil Society Organizations engaging with ASEAN.

As a thesis adviser, Saludadez demonstrates a broad range of methodological approaches across various social and communicative phenomena. They have supervised studies utilizing ethnomethodology to examine topics such as automated repository management, the communicative practices of women in IT leadership, and the social construction of inclusivity on digital platforms. Their supervision includes autoethnographic research regarding teacher identity, diasporic communication, and the integration of ASEAN perspectives in education. They have also overseen work employing ventriloquial analysis, symbolic interactionism, and rhetorical studies, covering subjects from student confession pages to child marriage practices on social media.

The breadth of their supervision is evident in the diverse contexts of their advisees, ranging from maritime security and amphibious warfare in the ASEAN region to the communicative practices of rice farmers in Midsayap, Cotabato. They have guided research into specialized areas such as the impact of Generative AI in multicultural classrooms, the role of film in history education, and the experiences of educators in allied medical programs during the transition to distance learning. Their supervision also extends to examining digital ageism, the communicative power of peace process documents, and the branding practices of non-profit organizations on social media. While some thesis entries in the repository lack substantive summaries or research content, the available data indicates a consistent interest in how communicative practices shape organizational, social, and political realities. Their most recent advised thesis, completed in 2026, focuses on the communicative practices of an educator integrating broadcasting experience into documentary filmmaking pedagogy to amplify marginalized voices.
